Xarray result

Source: R/result.R
XarrayResult-class.Rd

A statement is a Python expression evaluated with ds (the dataset) and xr (the module) in scope, plus any params. Evaluation happens at DBI::dbSendQuery(). A selection (sel(), isel(), indexing) is lazy there: it describes the cells and reads nothing. A statement that computes, such as a reduction (.mean()) or arithmetic, runs right then unless the data are dask-backed, and the max_cells guard sizes only its result, so it does not cover that computation. Rendering to the tidy data frame happens at the first DBI::dbFetch(): one row per cell, every coordinate as a column, exactly as xarray's to_dataframe().reset_index() gives it. DBI::dbGetQuery() is the two in one step.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'XarrayConnection,character'
dbSendQuery(conn, statement, ..., params = NULL)

# S4 method for class 'XarrayResult'
dbBind(res, params, ...)

# S4 method for class 'XarrayResult'
show(object)

# S4 method for class 'XarrayResult'
dbIsValid(dbObj, ...)

# S4 method for class 'XarrayResult'
dbGetStatement(res, ...)

# S4 method for class 'XarrayResult'
dbFetch(
  res,
  n = -1,
  ...,
  max_cells = getOption("xrdbi.max_cells", 1e+07),
  force = FALSE
)

# S4 method for class 'XarrayResult'
dbHasCompleted(res, ...)

# S4 method for class 'XarrayResult'
dbGetRowCount(res, ...)

# S4 method for class 'XarrayResult'
dbClearResult(res, ...)

Arguments

conn

an XarrayConnection

statement

a Python expression over ds (and xr)

...

unused

params

named list of values the statement refers to by name; see the Parameters section

object, dbObj, res

an XarrayResult

n

number of rows to fetch, -1 for all remaining

max_cells

guard threshold for the first fetch, default getOption("xrdbi.max_cells", 1e7)

force

bypass the guard

Value

  • dbSendQuery(): an XarrayResult

  • dbBind(): the result, invisibly, ready to fetch from the start

  • dbFetch(): a data frame of the next n rows

  • dbHasCompleted(), dbIsValid(): logical

  • dbGetRowCount(): the number of rows fetched so far

  • dbGetStatement(): the statement

  • dbClearResult(): TRUE, invisibly

  • show(): called for its output

Details

The first fetch is guarded: an xarray result above max_cells cells errors unless force = TRUE (see options(xrdbi.max_cells = )). Later fetches page through the same rows.

Slots

ptr

environment holding the evaluated Python object and the fetch state

statement

the Python expression

Parameters

params is a named list; each element becomes a Python variable of that name in the statement's scope, beside ds and xr, so dbGetQuery(con, "ds.sst.sel(lat=lat0, method='nearest')", params = list(lat0 = -60)) selects at -60. dbBind() evaluates the statement again with new values and restarts the fetch. Values become:

  • length-1 vectors: numpy scalars (wrap in I() to keep a 1-element array); longer vectors: 1-D numpy arrays. Factors become strings.

  • Date: datetime64[D]; POSIXct: datetime64[ns] as UTC, the way xarray stores times; NA becomes NaT

  • geometry (an sfc, the geometry column of an sf, or any wk vector): shapely geometries via WKB, as a numpy array; with a CRS, a geopandas GeoSeries carrying it (needs geopandas), the form xvec's extract_points() and zonal_stats() take

  • data frames: pandas DataFrames

  • reticulate Python objects: unchanged

Names must be Python identifiers; ds, xr and names starting with _xrdbi are reserved.

See also

xr_query() to write a statement from a structured selection; tbl() to compile one from dplyr verbs; xr_raster() and xr_chunks() to render the same statement other ways; the guard's options in xrdbi-package.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## needs a Python environment with xarray (see ?xrdbi)
f <- system.file("extdata/autotest/trmm.nc", package = "xrdbi")
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), f)
res <- dbSendQuery(con, "ds.pcp.isel(time=0)")
dbFetch(res, n = 5)
dbFetch(res, n = 5)
dbGetRowCount(res)
dbClearResult(res)

dbGetQuery(con, "ds.pcp.sel(latitude=slice(-15, -12), longitude=slice(-75, -72))")

## values from R, by name: the cells nearest two points
dbGetQuery(con,
  "ds.pcp.isel(time=0).sel(latitude=xr.DataArray(lats, dims='pt'),
    longitude=xr.DataArray(lons, dims='pt'), method='nearest')",
  params = list(lats = c(-15.1, -12.6), lons = c(-75.3, -72.8)))

## rebind and fetch again; method='nearest' also matches times that are
## not at midnight (OISST's are at 12:00, so an exact date would not)
res <- dbSendQuery(con, "ds.pcp.sel(time=t0, method='nearest')",
                   params = list(t0 = as.Date("2011-01-01")))
dbFetch(res, n = 3)
dbBind(res, list(t0 = as.Date("2011-01-02")))
dbFetch(res, n = 3)
dbClearResult(res)

## geometry: sf or wk vectors become shapely (a GeoSeries with a CRS);
## the .xvec accessor exists once xvec has been imported
reticulate::py_require(c("xvec", "geopandas"))
reticulate::import("xvec")
pts <- wk::xy(c(-75.3, -72.8), c(-15.1, -12.6), crs = "EPSG:4326")
dbGetQuery(con,
  "ds.pcp.xvec.extract_points(pts, x_coords='longitude', y_coords='latitude')",
  params = list(pts = pts))
dbDisconnect(con)
} # }
